introduction.text: The Fontana del Prigione is a historic fountain in Rome, notable for its Renaissance design, its association with Pope Sixtus V, and its role in the city’s water supply history.

history.description: Restoration of the ancient Aquedotto Alessandrino completed in 1587, which prompted the construction of new fountains.
Construction of the fountain by Domenico Fontana for Villa Montalto Peretti between 1587 and 1590.
In 1636 the Massimo family described the fountain’s statue as a prisoner.
The fountain was acquired by the Municipality of Rome in 1888.
Reconstruction of the fountain as the foundation of Via Genova in 1894-1895.
The fountain was disassembled again in 1923 and reassembled at its current location.
Restoration work carried out by the municipality in 2005-2006.

design.description: The fountain features a niche with two lesenes supporting a decorated pediment, lion heads, a central lion spouting water, six small columns, and travertine pillars with volutes.

art.description: The fountain originally included a group of marble statues: Apollo, a prisoner, Venus, and an aceless statue of Esculapio, now lost.
